title: Scripture plainly teaches God's foreknowledge: the prophets are its witnesses (Tertullian)
source_text: II. Sed mirum est homines divinam authoritatem Scripturae tribuentes, hoc in animum inducere posse. Nihil enim evidentius ex Scriptura colligitur, quam Deum futura quaelibet praenosse, quod manifestum faciunt quae in Scripturis habentur Prophetarum praedictiones. Nam ut scite Tertullianus, Praescientia Dei tot habet testes, quot Deus fecit Prophetas. Neque enim Prophetae potuerunt, inspirante Deo, ea praedicere quae post multa demum secula contigerunt, & ab hominibus libere sunt facta, nisi quae talia sunt ab aeterno Deo nota sunt.
pass_a_gloss: But it is wonderful that men attributing divine authority to Scripture, can bring their mind to this. For nothing is more evidently gathered from Scripture, than that God foreknew any future things whatever, which the predictions of the Prophets that are had in the Scriptures make manifest. For as Tertullian aptly says, The foreknowledge of God has as many witnesses, as God has made Prophets. For neither could the Prophets, God inspiring them, foretell those things which at length happened after many ages, and were done freely by men, unless such things were known to God from eternity.
pass_b_english: It is astonishing that people who grant Scripture divine authority can persuade themselves of this. Nothing is gathered more plainly from Scripture than that God knew beforehand every future thing, as the prophecies recorded in it make clear.

As Tertullian neatly puts it, 'God's foreknowledge has as many witnesses as God has made prophets.' The prophets, inspired by God, could not have foretold things that happened only many ages later and were done freely by human beings unless those things were known to God from eternity.

lemmas.latin: Praescientia Dei tot habet testes, quot Deus fecit Prophetas
lemmas.gloss: The foreknowledge of God has as many witnesses, as God has made Prophets

choices.why: The standard English term for God's knowing in advance; 'foreknowledge' is kept throughout for praescientia, with 'foresee' for praevidere.
